note: French typography requires a space before the question mark.
proposed_target: Devons-nous nous lever tôt demain matin ?
proposed_english: Do we have to get up early tomorrow morning?

note: Que dis-tu de... means 'How about...?', not specifically 'Do you feel like...'.
proposed_target: Que dis-tu de sortir faire une promenade ?
proposed_english: How about going out for a walk?

note: Standard punctuation requires a comma before the c'est clause.
proposed_target: Tout ce que je peux faire, c'est faire de mon mieux.
proposed_english: All I can do is do my best.

note: me nourrir means feed/support myself, not specifically buy food.
proposed_target: Tout ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est d'assez d'argent pour me nourrir.
proposed_english: All I need is enough money to feed myself.

proposed_target: Tout ce dont j'ai besoin, c'est d'un peu plus de temps.
proposed_english: All I need is a little more time.

note: le faire means 'do it', not 'do that'.
proposed_target: Tout ce que je veux, c'est une autre chance de le faire.
proposed_english: All I want is another chance to do it.

note: In standard French after Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est, the infinitive does not take de.
proposed_target: Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est appuyer sur ce bouton.
proposed_english: All you have to do is push this button.

note: In standard French after c'est here, remove de before the infinitive.
proposed_target: Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est nous rejoindre.
proposed_english: All you have to do is join us.

note: In standard French after c'est here, remove de before the infinitive.
proposed_target: Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est la rencontrer.
proposed_english: All you have to do is meet her.

note: In standard French after c'est here, remove de; faire de ton mieux directly means do your best.
proposed_target: Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est faire de ton mieux.
proposed_english: All you have to do is do your best.

note: In standard French after c'est here, remove de before the infinitive.
proposed_target: Tout ce que tu as à faire, c'est laver les assiettes.
proposed_english: All you have to do is wash the dishes.

note: Remove nonstandard de after c'est; noir sur blanc means explicitly/in writing, which English currently drops.
proposed_target: Tout ce que vous avez à faire, c'est l'écrire noir sur blanc.
proposed_english: All you have to do is put it in writing.

note: vous faire confiance is ambiguous between trusting yourselves and one another; make reciprocal meaning explicit for learners.
proposed_target: Tout ce que vous avez à faire, c'est vous faire confiance les uns aux autres.
proposed_english: All you need to do is trust each other.

note: franchement means frankly/openly; English 'frank enough' adds an 'enough' construction not present in French.
proposed_target: Les Américains disent franchement ce qu'ils pensent.
proposed_english: Americans openly say what they think.

note: French is an if-clause ('If you hurry...'), while English turns it into an imperative coordination.
proposed_target: Si tu te dépêches tu peux encore attraper ton train.
column6: you can still catch your train.

note: Direct learner translation is 'I really appreciate your help'; English 'I am much obliged' is unnecessarily formal/indirect.
